caption.scope: Simulator implementation of two-tier glucose counterregulation as described in Cryer 2013 (Cryer PE, J Clin Invest 123:1403-1405, 2013). Layer 1 — acute: catecholamine- and glucagon-driven glycogenolysis (t½ ≈ 60 min, T1D cap 0.4 vs ~5.0 in healthy individuals due to absent glucagon response; Cryer 2013 Table 1). Layer 2 — chronic: cortisol-mediated gluconeogenesis upregulation from sleep loss and illness (t½ ≈ 12 h). A HAAF gate (Hypoglycemia-Associated Autonomic Failure) attenuates acuteStress when repeated hypoglycemia accumulates, modeled after the Cryer 2013 hierarchy. Both layers converge with circadian cortisol, protein-glucagon, and the glycogen-dependent baseline onto a unified stressMultiplier; the liver then computes EGP = EGP0 · max(0, stressMultiplier − x3). Acute stress simultaneously depletes the hepatic glycogen pool, so prolonged counterregulation raises GNG compensation while glycogenolysis capacity falls.

variables.definition: rapid catecholamine + glucagon response — driven by hypoglycemia (Somogyi) and anaerobic exercise; t½ ≈ 60 min, capped at 0.4 in T1D
sustained cortisol elevation — driven by sleep loss (+0.06 per lost hour) and illness; t½ ≈ 12 h
HAAF gate: 0.3 + 0.7 · exp(-hypoArea / 30) — scales acuteStress down when repeated hypoglycemia accumulates
hepatic glycogen reserve as fraction 0–1 of the nominal 90 g pool; depleted by acuteStress, replenished at rest
unified hepatic drive >= 1; sum of glycogenBaseline, gngBaseline, effectiveAcuteStress, chronicStress, circadianCortisol, proteinGlucagon
hepatic glucose production rate; EGP0 = basal rate (~0.0161 × weight mmol/min for T1D); s = stressMultiplier; x3 = insulin EGP-suppression effect
glycogen-dependent EGP baseline: glycogenBaseline = 0.5·R + gngBaseline; gngBaseline = 0.5 + 0.25·(1-R) compensates falling glycogen via gluconeogenesis (Petersen 2004)
acuteStress · (0.6·R + 0.4) — glycogen-permissive weighting: 60 % from glycogenolysis, 40 % floor from sympathetic activation
HAAF-attenuated scale factor applied to acuteStress before summation into stressMultiplier
chronicStress accumulation rate: +0.06 per hour of sleep below target
dawn-phenomenon cortisol component: sine wave, peak 08:00, amplitude ≈ 0.15
amino-acid Hill-function glucagon response from the protein-glucagon pathway
computed hepatic glucose output — flows into plasma glucose pool Q1
